$comment: PRE-REGISTRATION — docs/14 § 5 criterion 5, written and committed before any ΔTTD from it exists.
Read it the way DECISIONS.md § D151's PRIMARY_CELLS is read: the point of the file is that it was
fixed first. § D139's bad-criterion list names choosing the reference arm, the budget or the cell
set after seeing a result, and § D151 § 8 names adding a cell after seeing one; this file is what
makes both checkable rather than promised.
The two cells are one declared Holm family and are NOT pooled with § D151's PRIMARY or SECONDARY
families, which § D151 § 3 forbids enlarging. `midtown-interfloor-1.5pct` is § D145's own operating
point and `lunch-two-way-1.5pct` is § D200's, so both refusals are directly comparable with what
this measures. Neither of those two entries is superseded by anything measured here.
What is new, and it is the honest reason to teach now rather than earlier: `demand.dayVariation`.
§ D156 found that the policy learned a busy/idle schedule because the shipped demand template
varied the level and never the directional split — it had nothing else to discriminate on. Cell 1
now varies the level BETWEEN runs (docs/14 § 2.3, wave 13 step 4) and cell 2 varies the mix WITHIN
a run as well (§ D169). Under the traffic-seed split every replication of both arms sees the same
day, so the day is common to the paired difference and cancels out of it (§ D206).
The budget is 200 — the top of CLAUDE.md's 50–200 band — and is NOT lowered if a census reveals a
ceiling under it. `benchmark/doubleDeck.ts` is the shipped precedent: a re-census dropped that
point's ceiling from 386 to 90, the pre-registered 200 was left at 200, and the point was published
UNQUOTABLE, because a budget chosen after seeing the answer is what a pre-registration exists to
prevent.
The two seeds are the repository's own, and that is deliberate rather than incidental. The run
seed and the training traffic seed are both BENCHMARK_SEED 20260726 — and a traffic seed equal to
the run seed selects exactly the streams the run already had, so the training traffic here IS the
traffic every published Midtown figure was measured on, byte for byte. The holdout traffic seed
20261537 is the disjoint holdout § D145, § D156 and § D200 each validated against. So the crowd
this policy is judged on is the crowd those three verdicts were taken on, and the run seed is held
across both, which is the thing docs/14 § 1.1 buys and none of the three had.
Reproduce with: elevator-sim tune --teaching packages/experiments/src/teaching/phase6c-midtown.teaching.json
